newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia to sell stake in nickel giant February 18.
newsitem.headline: Colombia to sell stake in nickel giant February 18.

text.p: The Colombian government will auction off its 46.58 stake in the sprawling Cerro Matoso nickel mine on February 18, the Bogota stock exchange said Friday.

It said the open auction would be held on all three of Colombia's stock exchanges at 1500 local/2000 GMT and that the government had set a base price of no less than 32,610 pesos per share for its remaining 5.38 million shares in the mine.
The government sold 2.32 percent of its equity in the mine to Cerro Matoso employees on Dec. 16 for 4.17 billion pesos.

Cerro Matoso ranks as the world's fourth largest nickel producer. South Africa's Gencor Ltd owns a controlling 52.3 percent stake in the mine, through its subsidiary Billiton, and has been mentioned among top possible bidders for the government's share.
The government said last year that it hoped to raise $100 million from the privatization of the mine, which produces about 65 million pounds of coal annually.
The base price set for the auction means that the government has upped the ante considerably, however, and now hopes to receive more than $160 million.

The auction-sale by Colombia's Sociedad Fiduciaria Industrial S.A., a branch of the government's Industrial Development Institute, is being managed by SBC Warburg Inc and Corfigan, a subsidiary of Colombia's Banco Ganadero.
